raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Clients built on the OpenAI Responses API (the openai SDK's `responses.*`, Codex) cannot use sgl-router today: it only serves chat completions. This adds `POST /v1/responses` to the router.

## Modifications

A Responses request is converted to a chat request at ingress and served by the existing `chat_completions` handler, so it is routed exactly like chat (tokenization, cache-aware routing, admission, retry, PD). The reply is converted back on the outer body, streaming or not.

- **Request**: string or item `input`; messages (`developer` → `system`), reasoning, function calls and outputs; text and image parts; `instructions`, `max_output_tokens`, `reasoning.effort`, `text.format` (JSON schema), `tool_choice`. Conversion works on `serde_json::Value`, so sglang chat extensions (`top_k`, `chat_template_kwargs`, …) pass through.
- **Tools**: `function`, plus the shapes Codex sends: `namespace` groups (flattened to `<ns>__<name>`) and `custom` freeform tools (a function with one `input` string, grammar appended to the description). Replies map back to namespaced `function_call` / `custom_tool_call` items, and history items of both kinds are accepted.
- **Streaming**: the spec event sequence with a gapless `sequence_number` (`response.created` → `in_progress` → item / part / delta / done events → `completed`, `incomplete` or `failed`); usage, including `cached_tokens`, is always present. An engine abort ends the Response as `failed`.
- **Unsupported, rejected with 400**: `previous_response_id`, `conversation`, `background` and stored prompts (the router is stateless; send the full conversation), and `top_logprobs`. `reasoning.effort` is passed through to the engine unchanged.
- **Errors**: engine errors are re-wrapped into the `{"error": {...}}` envelope; an upstream reply that cannot be read or parsed is a 502 via `ApiError::UpstreamStatus`.
- `src/protocol/sse.rs` is a small generic layer that rewrites a chat SSE body into another protocol's events (`SseTransducer`, `transduce_body`). It wraps the body produced by `proxy/sse.rs`, so timeouts, abort-on-disconnect and TTFT/ITL metrics are unchanged.

Built-in tools such as `web_search` are rejected with 400.

The companion PR for Anthropic `/v1/messages` (#42316) carries a byte-identical `protocol/sse.rs`; whichever lands second only needs a one-line rebase in `protocol/mod.rs`.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A: no model or kernel change.

Unit tests cover conversion, buffered and streamed replies, and the Codex tool shapes; `tests/proxy/responses_api.rs` drives requests end to end through a mock worker. `cargo test` (lib + proxy) and `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` pass.

Also validated against a live deployment: the official openai Python SDK's types (strict validation of every Response object and stream event), and Codex-style `namespace` / `custom` tool calls, streamed and buffered, including history replay.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A: no change to the chat path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

nodes.body: [P2] Tool calls are always marked `completed`, even when the output was cut off (`length`) or aborted, so a truncated call looks complete. Use `finish.item_status()` here and in `response.rs:66`?

[P2] Only one call is tracked, matched by `index`, which breaks two ways:
- Interleaved indices (0, 1, 0, 1) become four calls, the later two with made-up IDs, empty names and partial arguments.
- SGLang's Gemma 4 parser reuses one index for repeated calls to the same tool, so two separate calls merge into one.

Track calls by `id`, and attach chunks without an `id` to the call with that `index`?
[P2] Dropping the allow-list lets the model call tools the client excluded. Filter `tools` to the list, or reject?
[P2] The open item is dropped on failure: after streaming `"partial answer"`, `response.failed` has `output: []` and the item never gets `output_item.done`. Close it as `incomplete` first?

Only string system messages are merged. `instructions` plus a developer item with two `input_text` parts gives two leading system messages, which Qwen3.5 rejects. Flatten text-only parts before merging?

A `developer` item after the first turn becomes a `system` message mid-conversation, which some templates reject (e.g. Qwen3.5). Moving it to the top would reorder the history, so maybe send it as `user` instead?
nit: adjacent assistant messages are joined with no separator (`"A."` + `"B."` → `"A.B."`). Same for reasoning below.
nit: `input` is borrowed, so image parts (often large base64) are copied here and at L444. Taking `input` by value would avoid the copy.
